html:
Rani Lakshmibai was the queen of Jhansi, a small Maratha state in central India, who led her troops against the British in the Indian Rebellion of 1857 and died fighting in 1858.

Born in Varanasi and named Manikarnika, she married Gangadhar Rao, the raja of Jhansi. When he died in 1853 the couple's adopted son was refused the throne under the Doctrine of Lapse, the rule by which the East India Company took over states that lacked a natural heir. Jhansi was annexed in 1854.

When the rebellion broke out, she took charge of Jhansi. In 1858 a British force under Hugh Rose besieged and stormed the fort. She escaped on horseback, joined Tatya Tope, and together they seized the great fort of Gwalior. She was killed in battle near Gwalior in June 1858, in her late twenties.

Even Rose praised her courage. She became the best known symbol of Indian resistance, in songs, poems and films. In the Second World War, Subhas Chandra Bose named the women's unit of his army the Rani of Jhansi Regiment.
